analysis: Reviewed the two base_text units of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 819-1297 and 1298-1681). The PR changes visible in the patch excerpt are documentation-only: Autopilot waiting_inventory wording (lines 14-16), the `status` row now describing 'Also downloaded' and 'Downloads' output (line 781), and edits near base 819-820 / head 821-825 about Autopilot enrollment and prefetch. The excerpt is truncated, so the head side of the ranges 786-787 and 821-825 was not visible, and the base text I was given covers only lines 819-820 of those changes. The wording shifts toward the update's verified prefetch adding newly downloaded models to the Autopilot set automatically. This could weaken the earlier 'newly discovered/downloaded models do not enroll automatically' consent statement, but whether code enforces anything different is outside the supplied evidence. Nothing in this file affects controls from the threat model such as TB-002, TB-011, T-041, T-053, or the prefix-cache storage. I found no observable security regression, new attack surface, or invalidated assumption in the docs. Remaining integration questions: (1) Does the code behind the changed docs, for example the Autopilot prefetch that auto-adds downloaded models to the set, still honor operator consent and verified-hash checks? That code is not supplied here. (2) Do the new download usage and disk-free reporting fields in `status --json` expose anything sensitive? That is unverified but low risk, since they are local operator output. Because the patch excerpt is truncated, I am requesting only a light follow-up on the consent-semantics change.
